extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, editors, and readers interested in journalism/photography ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Discussion and guidelines about acceptable vs. unethical photographic manipulation in news/photojournalism, including the National Press Photographers Association (NPPA) Code of Ethics and community practical guidance on digital editing workflow and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be accurate and comprehensive in the representation of subjects.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be accurate and comprehensive in the representation of subjects." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain factual fidelity to what was photographed; do not alter an image such that it presents a different or misleading reality. Accuracy is the foundational obligation for news images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist being manipulated by staged photo opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Resist being manipulated by staged photo opportunities." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid participating in or accepting staged events that would distort the factual nature of a news image. Be wary of setups meant to produce a more dramatic shot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be complete and provide context; avoid stereotyping and bias.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be complete and provide context when photographing or recording subjects. Avoid stereotyping individuals and groups. Recognize and work to avoid presenting one's own biases in the work." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sufficient contextual detail so the image does not mislead; consciously guard against framing that reinforces stereotypes or personal bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat subjects with respect and consider vulnerable people compassionately.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Treat all subjects with respect and dignity. Give special consideration to vulnerable subjects and compassion to victims of crime or tragedy. Intrude on private moments of grief only when the public has an overriding and justifiable need to see." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance public interest against harm; avoid gratuitous exploitation of vulnerable subjects; intrusions must be justified by overriding public need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not intentionally contribute to, alter, or influence events while photographing.
rubrics_metrics.description: "While photographing subjects do not intentionally contribute to, alter, or seek to alter or influence events." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stage scenes, move subjects, or take actions that change the event you are documenting. Passive observation is required for news images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing must maintain integrity; don’t manipulate to mislead or misrepresent.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Editing should maintain the integrity of the photographic images' content and context. Do not manipulate images or add or alter sound in any way that can mislead viewers or misrepresent subjects." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine tonal/crop corrections for reproduction are acceptable; any edit that changes the content, meaning, or context (adding/removing elements, altering persons' appearance to mislead) is forbidden for news images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay or materially reward sources or subjects for participation.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not pay sources or subjects or reward them materially for information or participation." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary or material incentives that influence a subject's presence or behavior undermine independence and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept gifts, favors, or compensation from those who might influence coverage.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not accept gifts, favors, or compensation from those who might seek to influence coverage." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest and anything that creates the appearance of compromised independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not intentionally sabotage the efforts of other journalists.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Do not intentionally sabotage the efforts of other journalists." (NPPA Code of Ethics)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional conduct toward colleagues; do not interfere with others' reporting or dissemination of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive to ensure public business is conducted in public and defend access rights.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Strive to ensure that the public's business is conducted in public. Defend the rights of access for all journalists." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate for transparency and access so journalists can document public affairs without unnecessary restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a unique vision; remain engaged with current events and visual media.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Think proactively, as a student of psychology, sociology, politics and art to develop a unique vision and presentation. Work with a voracious appetite for current events and contemporary visual media." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate broad knowledge and a personal, ethical visual approach while staying grounded in factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strive for access and diversity of viewpoints in coverage.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Strive for total and unrestricted access to subjects, recommend alternatives to shallow or rushed opportunities, seek a diversity of viewpoints, and work to show unpopular or unnoticed points of view." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue comprehensive coverage and include underrepresented perspectives to avoid skewed reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid political, civic, or business involvements that compromise independence.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Avoid political, civic and business involvements or other employment that compromise or give the appearance of compromising one's own journalistic independence." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of outside activities that create real or perceived conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be unobtrusive and humble when dealing with subjects.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Strive to be unobtrusive and humble in dealing with subjects." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize intrusion; respect subjects' space and dignity while gathering images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the integrity of the photographic moment.
rubrics_metrics.description: "Respect the integrity of the photographic moment." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter a captured moment in ways that change its essential meaning; preserve the scene's authenticity when representing it as news.

rubrics_metrics.name: When unsure, seek counsel and continuously study craft and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.description: "When confronted with situations in which the proper action is not clear, seek the counsel of those who exhibit the highest standards of the profession. Photojournalists should continuously study their craft and the ethics that guide it." (NPPA Code of Ethics - ideally)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult editors, senior colleagues, or ethics codes when boundaries are ambiguous; ongoing education in technique and ethics is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor tonal/technical adjustments for reproduction are acceptable but must not change content.
rubrics_metrics.description: Community consensus and commenters' guidance: minor adjustments (levels, exposure, color balance, contrast, sharpening, dodging/burning to correct lighting) are common and acceptable if they do not materially change what is depicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: correcting overall exposure, fixing white balance, subtle contrast/curve adjustments, standard sharpening for print. These are analogous to traditional darkroom practices; intent should be enhancement for legibility/print quality, not alteration of meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add or remove major elements (inserting/removing people or objects) — that is unethical.
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple commenters emphasized that faking images by inserting or removing major portions is unethical and damages public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly prohibited for news images: cloning in/out people or objects, compositing elements from different events, erasing background elements that change context (e.g., removing protesters), or otherwise fabricating the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blackening backgrounds or radically altering backgrounds that change context is improper for news photos.
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters cite the firefighter photo where the background was blacked out or turned lurid orange as an example of crossing the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background removal/overly aggressive burning that eliminates contextual detail or misrepresents the scene is unacceptable for documentary/news images; such treatments may be acceptable in artistic/illustrative contexts if labeled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label heavily altered images as 'photo illustration' when not documentary.
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice from commenters: "Most often, this situation can be avoided by simply labeling the image as a 'photo illustration'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an image has been altered beyond routine correction or staged/constructed, explicitly label it so viewers understand it is not a documentary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow newsroom/publication rules and consult editors before making substantive edits.
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple comments: photographers who self-edit without consulting their employer can violate organizational rules; if rules prohibit a practice, breaking them can be grounds for dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know and follow your employer's technical and ethical policies; when in doubt, discuss intended edits with photo editors or layout staff to avoid surprises and maintain chain-of-custody/integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cropping is a legitimate compositional tool but must not be used to mislead.
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters: cropping is part of composition and acceptable unless done with intent to deceive (e.g., making a crowd look larger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cropping to strengthen framing and clarity; avoid cropping that removes essential contextual information in a way that changes the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject or flag severely degraded supplied files (e.g., severely underexposed JPGs) rather than perform destructive edits.
rubrics_metrics.description: From the posted 0-8 workflow: "If the image is supplied as JPG and is too horribly under-exposed (or entirely washed out), reject it or skip this and all other steps."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When source files lack adequate data, do not attempt extreme fixes that could create misleading results; request better source material or decline the photo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard digital toning workflow and constraints (order and non-destructive methods).
rubrics_metrics.description: A step-by-step recommended workflow (commenter's list 0–8): 0) Intent: edits only to ensure printed quality and not significantly change content; 1) Analyze grey levels and neutrals; 2) Crop if needed; 3) Adjust levels for exposure; 4) Correct neutral color casts; 5) Create RGB s-curve for contrast; 6) Dodge and burn non-destructively (use history brush technique); 7) Adjust black for press reproduction; 8) Sharpen consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do these steps in order using non-destructive techniques (histories, layers, consistent actions/macros). The goal is reproduction fidelity, not artistic transformation. Use the same parameters for press consistency and avoid ad-hoc destructive edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different standards for news (documentary) vs. editorial/illustrative images.
rubrics_metrics.description: Community guidance: "News images are one thing, editorial/illustrative images are another." Treat news images with stricter limits on manipulation than images intended as illustration or art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the image's purpose is editorial/illustrative or for a contest where stylistic edits are allowed, different practices may be permissible — but the image must be labeled and the publication/contest rules followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to contest/publication rules; be aware awards panels may have stricter standards.
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments discuss awards being stripped by fellow photographers and contest rules differing from newsroom rules ("if the rules say 'Don't do X' and you do X and get fired don't complain").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting to contests or publications, verify their rules on digital manipulation; what is acceptable in one venue may disqualify you in another.
